page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the n4 family, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory. The processing power is delivered by an Intel CPU featuring 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, supported by a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The hardware profile features advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves average performance in single-core metrics, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1657.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1836.0. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression (28.31 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (11.95 GB/sec) also fall within the average range. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance is rated poor at 1736.79, and the Geekbench multi-core score is weak at 2242.0. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 17.81 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 11.0 GB/sec, both categorized as poor. Passmark database operations (1006.28) and software compilation with Clang (2253.0) also demonstrate poor performance.

The n4-highcpu-2 presents a specific resource-density tradeoff, offering dedicated Intel CPU execution with advanced matrix and vector instruction sets but with a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that require modern instruction sets (such as AMX or AVX-512) but do not demand large memory footprints or high memory bandwidth. Due to the poor multi-core scaling and weak database performance, this instance is not suited for memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded processing. It is best aligned with lightweight single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 compute-focused instance featuring 2 dedicated Intel vCPUs (1 physical core, 2 threads) and 4.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The hardware supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. Performance benchmarks show average single-core execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1836.0 and average single-threaded compression speeds. However, multi-core and memory-bound benchmarks are weak to poor, with memory write bandwidth limited to 11.0 GB/sec and a multi-core Geekbench score of 2242.0. This instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound, single-threaded tasks that leverage modern vector instructions without requiring large memory capacities. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale computational tasks.
